references.text: Jesus had resolved to go to Jerusalem, and when the village rejected him, he went on to another village in keeping with that decision.
Jesus gave similar instructions to the seventy: When a town does not welcome you, go out into its streets and shake the dust from your feet. The principle of moving on when rejected is repeated here.
Jesus instructs the disciples to leave houses or towns that do not receive them and to shake the dust from their feet—the same principle of moving on from rejection.
Jesus says that when they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. This aligns with going on to another village after being rejected.
Jesus was rejected in Nazareth but walked away through the crowd—he did not respond with retaliation but moved on, just as here.
Jesus traveled around Galilee and avoided Judea because the Jews were seeking to kill him. This shows the same pattern of moving on to other places rather than confronting rejection with force.
